title: 'ok' vs 'ok.'
hook_frame: Notebook page. The sketched phone lights up; a grey bubble 'ok.' lands in the thread with Jess. On-screen text: ok vs ok. The sticker TEXTING, DECODED · 1/7 is already in the corner. No voice until 0.7 s.

beats.screen: Real footage taped on the page: a woman reading her phone in bed, lit by the screen. Text: ok vs ok.

beats.voice: 'ok.' With the period. Congratulations. You're in trouble.
beats.draw: circle around the period, red marker

beats.screen: A sketched thumb types 'ok', stops, then adds the period; a timeline strip appears under the bubble: typed · paused · added .
beats.voice: They typed 'ok'. Paused. Went back for the period. Nobody does that by accident.
beats.control: calm and deliberate, a clear beat after 'paused', the last sentence drier
beats.draw: bracket under the strip, label 'the pause'

beats.screen: Cut-away beside the phone: the question 'dinner at 8?' and three replies drawn one by one: okay / ok / ok.
beats.voice: Same question. Three answers. One is a threat.

beats.screen: Same cut-away; a handwritten label appears beside each reply as it is said
beats.voice: 'okay': happy. 'ok': busy. 'ok.': you forgot something. Good luck.
beats.control: slower on the last reply, 'good luck' flat and sympathetic
beats.draw: labels: happy / busy / you forgot something
beats.sound: marker x3, tick on the last

beats.screen: Extreme close-up of the period on the page
beats.voice: Except. One kind of person breaks this rule.
beats.control: half a second of silence first, then quieter, like a secret

phrases.say: One kind of person breaks this rule.

beats.screen: A second sketched thread, 'Dad': every message ends with a period; three of them get circled
beats.voice: Dads. Bosses. People who sign their texts. Their 'ok.' is just 'ok'. Pattern first.
beats.control: warm, a little fond, a smile in the voice on 'sign their texts', firm on 'pattern first'
beats.draw: three circles, then the words PATTERN FIRST written large

beats.screen: The test: two sketched phones side by side. A: Jess's thread, no periods anywhere, then 'ok.'. B: Dad's thread, periods everywhere, then 'ok.'
beats.voice: Now you. A… or B? Careful. One of them is your dad.
beats.control: inviting, then straight-faced; a pause after 'B'; do not rush

phrases.say: One of them is your dad.

beats.screen: Reveal: A circled; Jess's earlier bubbles highlighted to show no periods
beats.voice: A. First period she's ever used. Dad's just Dad.
beats.control: quiet and certain, the last three words with a shrug

beats.screen: The same taped clip, played slowly so the last frame is frame 1 (the loop); 2/7 · Left on read writes on after the last word
beats.voice: Bonus. A lone 'k' is a door closing. On your face. Two of seven: left on read.
beats.control: lighter, a promise; 'on your face' said kindly; ends on a small upward note

phrases.say: A lone 'k' is a door closing.
phrases.tts: A lone K is a door closing.

phrases.say: Two of seven: left on read.
phrases.tts: Two of seven. Left on read.

test.a: 'ok.' from Jess, who never uses periods
test.why: It is the first period she has ever used; the change from her pattern is the message.

bonus: A lone 'k' is a door closing. On your face.
bridge: Two of seven: left on read.
teaches_line: the period. One character decides what 'ok' means, and the sender's own pattern decides the character.
pinned: A or B? Tell me which one you'd have guessed, and whether you're a period person.
